subject: Including 'individuals' as categorical variable in Lavaan: necessary?

messages.author: b430763ad49e6cd0
messages.subject: Including 'individuals' as categorical variable in Lavaan: necessary?
parts:
How does Lavaan know that each row in my data belongs to a different individual? Is that done automatically internally? I am asking this, as I am making a panel model and wonder if Lavaan 'understands' that my data is from 100+ individuals. For a latent growth curve model, I would have the same question.

I remember from linear mixed modeling (covariance pattern models) in SAS, that I needed to explicitly say what variable indicated this. As an example of this, see the picture below. Here, subject = patient tells SAS that the patient variable indicates a different subject. 



Thanks,

messages.author: ad188126f9138663
messages.subject: Re: Including 'individuals' as categorical variable in Lavaan: necessary?
parts:
Amonet,
  Is it possible that you are using the term 'individual' in two distinct sense that may be leading to confusion?  Lower level observational units are always represented by a single row.  Higher level units into which the lower level units are grouped are identified by a grouping variable in long format but not wide format.

  The word individual can refer to lower level units or it can refer to people who, in your case, appear to be the higher level units by which the lower level observations are grouped.

   For a growth curve model, you probably want to configure your data into wide format.  There will be one row for the higher level units and the lower level units will be represented by different variables in the same row.  This allows you to model the covariances of all the variables across the higher level units.

Keith
